content.user_title: Verify Completion Claims Before Reporting Success
content.value_statement: AI coding agents can overstate completion when checks were not freshly run. This skill requires fresh evidence before success claims, commits, pull requests, or task handoffs.
actual_capabilities: Prompts agents to identify the command that proves a completion claim.
Requires fresh verification before positive status statements.
Guides agents to read output, exit codes, and failure counts.
Separates tests, builds, lint checks, and requirements review.
Encourages red-green regression validation for bug fixes.
Requires diff review after delegated agent reports.
limitations: Does not run verification commands by itself.
Does not define project-specific test, build, or lint commands.
Cannot prove correctness beyond available verification output.
May slow replies when evidence is missing.

use_cases.title: Confirm a Fix Before Closing Work
use_cases.description: Require the agent to rerun the failing test and report the actual result before saying the fix is complete.

use_cases.title: Prepare Safer Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Make completion claims depend on fresh build, test, lint, and requirement evidence before opening or updating a pull request.

use_cases.title: Review Delegated Agent Work
use_cases.description: Check diffs and verification evidence after a delegated agent reports success, instead of accepting the report at face value.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Completion Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before saying a task is done.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before you claim this task is complete, identify the verification command, run it fresh, read the full output, and report the evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Bug Fix Verification
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after changing code for a reported defect.
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify the original bug is fixed. Run the specific failing check, then run the relevant broader checks. Report failures plainly.

prompt_templates.title: Pull Request Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before creating or updating a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the diff, requirements, tests, lint, and build status. Only state pull request readiness when fresh evidence supports it.

prompt_templates.title: Delegated Work Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after another agent reports success.
prompt_templates.prompt: Do not trust the delegated success report alone. Inspect the VCS diff, verify changed behavior, run required checks, and state the actual status.

output_examples.input: The agent is about to say all tests pass after editing a component.
output_examples.output: The agent first runs the test command, reads the result, and reports the passing count or the remaining failures.

output_examples.input: A delegated agent reports that it completed a refactor.
output_examples.output: The agent reviews the diff, checks that requested files changed, runs verification, and reports only evidence-backed status.

output_examples.input: A bug fix appears correct after code inspection.
output_examples.output: The agent verifies the original symptom, runs related checks, and avoids saying fixed until the evidence supports that claim.

best_practices: Pair every completion claim with command output and exit status.
Verify the original failure mode, not only broad checks.
Report unknown or failing checks plainly instead of using optimistic wording.
anti_patterns: Saying work is done because code changed.
Treating linter success as build or test success.
Accepting delegated agent success without reviewing diff and evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It tells the agent to choose and run the appropriate verification commands using available tools.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written as tool-neutral guidance for AI coding assistants.

faq.question: What counts as valid completion evidence?
faq.answer: Fresh command output, exit status, failure counts, diff review, and checklist results can support a claim.

faq.question: Does a passing linter prove the build works?
faq.answer: No. The skill treats lint, tests, build, and requirements as separate verification signals.

faq.question: Why does the skill mention delegated agents?
faq.answer: Delegated reports can be wrong. The main agent should verify diffs and behavior before relying on them.

faq.question: When should this skill be used?
faq.answer: Use it before success claims, commits, pull requests, handoffs, or any statement that work is complete.
